title: Writing questions
lede: Where questions live, how to make one, and the tagging rule that is not optional here.

blocks.text: Questions live in the question bank. Get there from the **Questions** menu at the top of any page, or from **Create Questions** on the portal home page. A question is an object in the bank. An assessment is a selection of those objects.

blocks.title: Tag every question with at least one category
blocks.text: The software will not force you to do this. JABSOM does. An untagged question is invisible to category reporting, which is how the school looks at performance by topic across a course and across years.

You can tag while writing a question using the **Add or Remove Category** button, then search or scroll the tree and click the green plus sign. To fix a batch of untagged questions, tick their checkboxes in the questions table, choose **Questions Bulk Edit Options** at the bottom of the screen, then **Change Category Assignments**.

blocks.title: Apply tags, but leave the tree alone
blocks.text: The category tree is shared across every course and about nine years of historical items. Renaming or moving a node quietly changes what past reports mean. Your account is set to restricted on Categories for that reason. If your course needs a category that does not exist, ask OME to add it.

items: Set your fonts first. See [Set your preferences first](#preferences).
**Partial Credit** on a multiple-answer question also caps how many choices a student can pick. Two correct answers means they can select two.
**+/- Partial Credit** adds points for correct picks and subtracts for wrong ones. Say so in the stem if you use it, so students do not guess blind.
Fill in the Blank allows up to 15 blanks per question. Separate acceptable alternative spellings with a vertical pipe.
